summary: The network administrator for Shrewsbury Public Schools emphasizes the importance of E-Rate for maintaining and improving the network infrastructure for their district, which serves 6,000 students. They argue that reducing or eliminating E-Rate would force districts to divert funding from other programs and student needs to pay for broadband infrastructure, potentially impacting other programs and student needs.

claims.argument: Reducing or eliminating E-Rate would force districts to divert funding from other programs and student needs to pay for broadband infrastructure
claims.evidence_quote: As a network administrator for Shrewsbury Public Schools in Massachusetts, I see firsthand how important E-Rate is to keeping our schools connected. Our district serves roughly 6,000 students, and E-Rate has helped us maintain and improve the network and wireless infrastructure they and our staff depend on every day.
